1034.body:
## What happens

`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts` → **"Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs"** (test declared at `:203`, step 6 `等待修复并恢复调用`, body at `:314`) fails at `test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:332`:

```
  1) [mocked] › ../test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:203:1 › journey-custom-mcp.spec › Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs › 6. 等待修复并恢复调用

    Error: expect(received).toBeGreaterThan(expected)

    Expected: > 2
    Received:   2

      330 |       expect(terminal.status, terminal.error).toBe("completed");
      331 |       const recovered = await invocations();
    > 332 |       expect(recovered.length).toBeGreaterThan(before);
          |                                ^
```

Everything before the assertion in step 6 succeeds: the repair card `执行受阻` shows `等待 MCP 修复` with the disabled source id, `GET /api/sessions/<id>/mcp/invocations` stays at 2 while blocked, the server is re-enabled, `已修复，重新检查` is clicked, and `waitForRunTerminal` returns `completed`.

What the run then shows: the assistant's last message in that run is `MCP RECOVERED`, which the scripted model only emits **after** its `mcp_recovered_call` step (`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:243-247`):

```ts
[
  { tool: "mcp_readiness", arguments: { action: "wait", reason: "This task requires the selected echo source", sourceIds: [second.id] } },
  { tool: "mcp_recovered_call", arguments: { sourceId: second.id, toolId: second.toolId, input: { text: "mcp recovered" } } },
  { text: "MCP RECOVERED" },
],
```

So the scripted model did emit `mcp_recovered_call`, and the run continued past it, but no MCP invocation was recorded for that turn: `/api/sessions/<id>/mcp/invocations` still lists exactly the 2 invocations from the earlier runs (`custom-cbf8e…`, `custom-cea28…`), and the captured trace resource `0000f751….json` holds the same 2. The recovered call therefore never reached `McpSourceCatalog`/broker (`packages/artifact-manager/src/mcp-workspace-tools.ts` `mcpReadiness.invoke`), and the failure is silent to the user: the run completes and the message claims recovery.

## Where it is seen (evidence only)

The same journey, same assertion, fails on three unrelated heads:

| run | job | head | shard window (UTC) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [42619667305](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42619667305) | [129188246374](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42619667305/job/129188246374) | `9bf5077f7b` (#857 tip) | 13:38–13:58 failure |
| [42622133086](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42622133086) | [129181494939](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42622133086/job/129181494939) | `87c5da950b` (`codex/conversation-proxy-resources`) | 13:39–13:59 failure |
| [42615122979](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42615122979) | [129160327871](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42615122979/job/129160327871) | `127bb1fdef` (merge queue, `pr-1005`) | 12:34–12:54 failure |

It also passes on other heads in the same window, including main running the journey while the two 13:3x failures were in flight:

- main `c3678320ac`: run [42621321893](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42621321893) job [129188930633](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42621321893/job/129188930633), `✓ 21 … Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs (44.4s)` at 13:39:17Z, shard success (13:34–13:49).
- main `9feafa2730`: run [42562181452](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42562181452) job [128981184690](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42562181452/job/128981184690), `✓ 21` at 04:38:35Z. That shard job is red overall because of a different journey (`journey-first-run.spec.ts:59`), so the shard verdict alone does not describe this journey.

`L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config)` outcomes for completed runs created between 11:30Z and 14:00Z (jobs read one by one; cancelled runs excluded): **3 failure / 16 success**, and the three failures are the table above. Two of the green runs are `dev2/fix/upload-windows-reserved-names` `0c5f26ab03` (13:33:34Z) and `dev/884-bug-comparing-two-binary-artifact-versio` `cefe1ebd79` (13:25:34Z).

## Not caused by the #857 diff

#857 (`9bf5077f7b`) changes exactly two files, `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` and `services/api/src/runs/index.test.ts` (+210/−23); the merge ref `fdf61b56798086e573368bc82120e91e8c5cc52b` for its failing job has parents `9feafa27` + `9bf5077f` and nothing else. The two other failing heads carry none of that diff. The failing journey exercises custom-MCP registration, the repair wait and `mcp_recovered_call` — not the scheduler's delayed retry pass. #857 is linked only because its shard run is one of the three observations, not as the cause.

## What is not yet known

Whether this is a product race (the recovered call is dropped or rejected after `catalog.refresh`, so a real user also loses the recovered invocation while the message claims it ran) or a test that stops waiting too early (it asserts the invocation list immediately after the terminal state). The two need different fixes, and the 3-of-19 rate above is the only discriminator so far: a deterministic loss is a product gap, an occasional one points at the wait.

Not run: local reproduction of the journey (20 consecutive runs on a local stack). The stack could not be started in the reporting environment — the pnpm store lives on a read-only home, the pinned Chromium download did not complete, and the JiuwenSwarm virtualenv install had not finished when this was filed. No code was changed for this report.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues (terms: `inapplicable`, `os:linux`, `platform skip`, `node --test windows`, `test discovery`, `silently skipped`, `host mismatch`) and did not find this behavior reported.
- [x] Verified still present on `main` at the commit listed under *Version Information*.
- [x] Environment information and a self-contained minimal reproduction are included below.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

When a test file declares an OS tag that the current host does not match, the package-level compatibility shim makes every registration call a no-op, so the file registers **zero** test cases — and `node --test` still prints `pass`, reports `skipped 0`, and exits `0`. Nothing in the output says the file was excluded because of its `os:` tag, so "ran nothing" and "ran and passed" are indistinguishable to the developer running the suite locally.

This affects the **direct** execution path only (`node --test <file>`, i.e. a package's own `"test": "node --import tsx --test \"src/**/*.test.ts\""` script). The shared plan path used by CI is not affected — see *Root-cause code references*.

### Root-cause code references

`test/support/tagged/compat.mjs`:

- **lines 19–22** — `declares()` treats a declared group as an allowlist: if a file declares any `os:` tag, only the declared hosts pass.
- **lines 45–52** — `createTest()` consults the host at line 48 (`hostPlatform(process.platform)` / `hostArch(process.arch)`) and returns `inapplicable()` at line 49 when the host is not in the declared set.
- **lines 30–36** — `inapplicable()` returns `{ ...native, test: declaration, it: declaration, describe: declaration, ...hooks }`, where `declaration` is `() => {}` and `declaration.skip`/`.todo`/`.only` are the *same* no-op. Every `test(...)` call is discarded, and an explicit `.skip(...)` request is discarded with it.

The comment at **lines 24–29** documents registering nothing as deliberate ("Registering nothing is what those files did before they were tagged"). The problem reported here is not that design decision — it is the observable outcome: the built-in runner counts the *file* as one test, so an excluded file is indistinguishable from a file whose cases all passed.

Contrast with the layers that do report, which is why this reads as a residual gap rather than intended behavior:

| location | behavior |
|---|---|
| `test/support/tagged/plan.mjs:88` | throws `EMPTY_SELECTION: no test instances selected` when a plan selects nothing |
| `test/support/tagged/plan.mjs:76` | plan selection is by tags only and never reads the host |
| `test/support/tagged/environment.mjs:47–49` | `preflight()` records a `HOST_MISMATCH` problem per entry when the plan target is not the host |
| `test/support/tagged/node.mjs:40` | the registry path refuses direct use outright: *"direct node --test would not enforce the frozen plan"* |
| `test/support/tagged/compat.mjs:49` | silent zero registration |

`compat.mjs:46` shows the two paths are disjoint: when the shared run has installed the registry symbol (`node-collect.mjs:22` → `node.mjs:24`), `createTest` delegates to the registry path and the host gate is never reached.

### Minimal reproduction

Save this as `os-tag-probe.mjs` in the repository root and run it. It needs no `node_modules`, no `tsx`, and no service — it imports the repository's own shim.

```js
// os-tag-probe.mjs
import * as native from 'node:test';
const { createTest } = await import('./test/support/tagged/compat.mjs');

const VARIANTS = {
  A: ['category:ut', 'os:linux'],                    // what the default branch declares today
  B: ['category:ut', 'os:linux', 'os:windows'],
  C: ['category:ut'],                                // no os: group declared at all
};

const tags = VARIANTS[process.env.PROBE_GROUP];
const t = createTest(import.meta.url, { tags });

console.log(
  `OBS tags=${tags.join(',')} host=${process.platform}/${process.arch} node=${process.version} ` +
  `returned_test_is_native=${t.test === native.test} test_is_describe=${t.test === t.describe} ` +
  `test_skip_is_test=${t.test.skip === t.test}`
);

t.test('probe-case-one', () => console.log('CASE_RAN probe-case-one'));
t.test('probe-case-two', () => console.log('CASE_RAN probe-case-two'));
```

```bash
for G in A B C; do PROBE_GROUP=$G node --test os-tag-probe.mjs; echo "exit=$?"; done
```

One file, one runner, one host — only the `tags` array differs between the three groups.

### Actual behavior

Group A, verbatim on a Windows host:

```text
# OBS tags=category:ut,os:linux host=win32/x64 node=v22.23.4 returned_test_is_native=false test_is_describe=true test_skip_is_test=true
# Subtest: os-tag-probe.mjs
ok 1 - os-tag-probe.mjs
1..1
# tests 1
# pass 1
# fail 0
# skipped 0
exit=0
```

Neither `CASE_RAN` line appears: **0 of the 2 declared cases ran**, `# skipped 0`, exit code 0, and no line mentions the platform or the tag. With the default spec reporter — what a developer actually looks at:

```text
✔ os-tag-probe.mjs (88.6081ms)
ℹ tests 1
ℹ pass 1
ℹ skipped 0
```

Groups B and C, verbatim tails from the same command:

```text
# OBS tags=category:ut,os:linux,os:windows host=win32/x64 node=v22.23.4 returned_test_is_native=true test_is_describe=false test_skip_is_test=false
# CASE_RAN probe-case-one
# CASE_RAN probe-case-two
# tests 2
# pass 2
# skipped 0
```

```text
# OBS tags=category:ut host=win32/x64 node=v22.23.4 returned_test_is_native=true test_is_describe=false test_skip_is_test=false
# CASE_RAN probe-case-one
# CASE_RAN probe-case-two
# tests 2
# pass 2
# skipped 0
```

| Group | Declared tags | `createTest()` returns | named cases executed | `# tests` | `# skipped` | exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | `os:linux` only | `inapplicable()` no-op | **0** | 1 (the file itself) | 0 | 0 |
| B | `os:linux` + `os:windows` | native `node:test` | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| C | no `os:` declared | native `node:test` | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |

Stability: the A/B/C set was run 3 times with identical results (A always `# tests 1 / # pass 1 / # skipped 0` with 0 `CASE_RAN`; B and C always `# tests 2` with 2). Group A also reproduced unchanged under Node v20.12.2 on the same host (`# tests 1`, `# pass 1`, `# skipped 0`, no `CASE_RAN`), so this is not tied to one Node minor.

### Expected behavior

Groups B and C are correct. Group A should not be able to read as a pass. Either:

- the file is reported as skipped with a reason naming host and tag, e.g. `# skipped 1` plus `platform-inapplicable: host windows/amd64 is not declared by os:linux`; or
- the summary distinguishes "0 cases, excluded by tag" from "cases ran and passed".

An assertion that silently never executes is worse than one that fails, because it also silently satisfies any "all tests pass" gate built on the exit code.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

| item | value |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 11, `10.0.22631.6199`, x64 |
| Shell used for the repro | Git Bash / MSYS2 `MINGW64_NT-10.0-22631 3.6.5` |
| Node.js (primary) | `v22.23.4`, the version the project pins |
| Node.js (cross-check) | `v20.12.2`, same group-A outcome |
| `process.platform` / `process.arch` | `win32` / `x64` → `hostPlatform` = `windows`, `hostArch` = `amd64` (`test/support/tagged/environment.mjs:17–18`) |
| Runner | Node's built-in test runner via `node --test` (TAP and `spec` reporters both shown) |
| Dependencies installed | none required for the probe |
| Services / devices / credentials | none involved |
| Repository revision | `main` at `7caff0e156a00800df6d5cb01bf95f81ea1f7a9a` |

## Additional Information

**How many files this covers on the default branch.** Measured at the commit above:

```bash
git grep -l "tagged/compat.mjs" origin/main | wc -l                    # 619  (files using the shim)
git grep -l '"os:linux"'    origin/main > linux.txt
git grep -l '"os:windows"'  origin/main > windows.txt
git grep -l "tagged/compat.mjs" origin/main > imports.txt
comm -23 <(sort imports.txt | grep -Fxf linux.txt) \
         <(sort imports.txt | grep -Fxf windows.txt) | wc -l            # 538  (shim + linux-only declared)
```

So 538 of the 619 files that use the shim register zero cases when run directly on a Windows host. They concentrate in `services/api` (146), `apps/web` (120), `apps/desktop` (85), `services/runner` (30), `services/launcher` (18), and 139 more spread over the remaining 35 package/directory groups — including `packages/specialist/src/builtins.test.ts`.

**What this report does not claim.**

1. **It is not a CI problem.** `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs:25,28` set `os: 'linux'` for every rule, targets derive from that field (line 63), and `.github/workflows/` contains no `windows` reference at all. CI never reaches `compat.mjs`'s host gate (`compat.mjs:46`), and plans select by tags alone (`plan.mjs:76`). No CI result changes because of this.
2. **It is not claimed to happen on Linux.** On `linux/amd64` the declared set contains the host, so `declares()` passes and native `node:test` is returned. That is read from `environment.mjs:17–18` + `compat.mjs:48`; it was not measured here, since only one Windows host was available.
3. **It is not a claim that Windows is a supported test host.** The profiles say it is not. The question is what a developer should see when they run the suite on an unsupported host anyway.
4. **It is not a product or agent-runtime defect.** Only `test/support/tagged/` registration behavior is involved; no runtime code path is implicated.
5. The 538 figure is a static tag scan. It does not mean those files' assertions would fail on Windows — only that none of them execute there.

**Suggested improvement.** The smallest option stays inside `inapplicable()`: instead of returning only no-ops, register exactly one skipped case, e.g.

```js
native.test('platform-inapplicable',
  { skip: `host ${hostPlatform(process.platform)}/${hostArch(process.arch)} not declared by ${declaredTags}` },
  () => {});
```

The tally then shows `# skipped 1` with the reason, while still running no real assertions — this keeps the documented intent of lines 24–29 and removes the false green. If registering a case is considered too invasive for this path, emitting a single diagnostic line naming the file and the unmet tag would already make the two outcomes distinguishable.

Whether Windows/macOS should become supported test hosts at all is a separate decision, and per `profiles.mjs` the compliant lever for that is adding targets, not per-file `os:` tags.

Related closed issue **#126** ("Consolidate test entry points and enforce complete test discovery") states the principle this residual gap runs against: *"a successful command must not conceal missing, unsupported, or unexecuted tests."*

Filed as a report only — no code change is proposed or attached, and no branch or PR is involved.

## Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, default branch `main`, commit `7caff0e156a00800df6d5cb01bf95f81ea1f7a9a` (2026-11-09).
- File under analysis: `test/support/tagged/compat.mjs`, blob `b8b9e2c74bea5e2f647e37a42527de8ccf1ba832`.
- Supporting files read at the same revision: `test/support/tagged/plan.mjs`, `test/support/tagged/environment.mjs`, `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs`, `test/support/tagged/node.mjs`, `test/support/tagged/node-collect.mjs`.
- Node.js used for the reproduction: `v22.23.4` (project-pinned); cross-checked with `v20.12.2`.
- No package version participates in the outcome; the probe imports no dependencies.
1042.title: [Bug]: Platform-inapplicable tests silently register zero cases in direct node:test execution

1049.author: JinhZhao
1049.body:
## 1. Summary

`europe-pmc_prepare_paper_download` and `pubmed_prepare_paper_download` resolve an open-access PMC
PDF by asking the **PMC OA Web Service**
(`https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/utils/oa/oa.fcgi`), which is the value of
`data_sources.ncbi.pmc_oa` in `config/external-urls.json` on the current default branch. That
endpoint no longer exists at the provider: **both** PMCIDs we requested return **HTTP 404** — one
unambiguously open access (row A1) and one not (row A2) — and the tool therefore cannot produce a
download candidate at all. We tested two identifiers, not the corpus; §11 states the sample.

The two layers are distinct and we state them separately (`SD` below means this repository,
`openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`):

* **External trigger — not attributed to SD.** NCBI announced on **2026-02-12** ("Changes to PMC
  Article Dataset Distribution Services Coming in 2026", NCBI Insights) that the **PMC OA Web
  Service API is retired as of August 2026**, with the PMC Cloud Service as its successor. No
  upstream action could keep a retired provider API answering, and we do not treat the retirement
  itself as an SD defect.
* **The two SD-side issues we are reporting, as one report.**
  1. *Endpoint dependency*: the shipped default configuration still points at the retired endpoint,
     and `_pmc_pdf_candidate` has no other route, so a provider-side change removed the whole
     download capability instead of degrading it.
  2. *Failure attribution*: the resulting 404 reaches the model as `NOT_FOUND / retryable:false` —
     **record-level vocabulary**. In the gateway a 404 is recorded as `failureScope="unknown"` (no
     endpoint-level verdict is produced for it), and the client layer then derives the code from the
     error *text* rather than from that field, so nothing in the result says "the configured service
     is gone". An agent therefore reads a dead endpoint as an absent document and records a gap in
     the literature instead of an outage — which is what we observed for both identifiers tried,
     open access and not.

These are one problem from the agent's point of view: the flattening is what turns a broken locator
into a wrong scientific conclusion. This is a configuration-and-error-attribution issue, not a
scheduling or tool-lifecycle issue: in the run we investigated, registration, catalog discovery,
deferred-tool promotion, model visibility, broker admission and the outbound request all worked as
designed.

## 2. Affected SD component and version

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Repository | `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` |
| Branch / commit verified | `main` @ `5c765cd0a2539b4b22baab32f1bc9b84fb4a21f3` (committed 2026-11-09T22:07:09Z) |
| Component | bundled gateway MCP server `biomed` (`services/gateway/…/public_biomed_mcp.py`), its source descriptor `packages/mcp-sources/src/public-biomed.ts` (`europe-pmc`, `pubmed`), the URL configuration `config/external-urls.json`, and the provider-error path `services/gateway/…/http_errors.py` → `services/api/src/mcp/node-client.ts` |
| Affected tools | `europe-pmc_prepare_paper_download`, `pubmed_prepare_paper_download` (both funnel into `_pmc_pdf_candidate`) |
| Introduced by | `9fa6607c729f` (2026-08-14, "first commit") — the only commit whose diff adds or removes `oa.fcgi` in that file (`git log -S"oa.fcgi" -- config/external-urls.json`) |
| Last commit touching the file | `d79e204d4b99` (author 2026-11-05, committed 2026-11-06) — "fix(gateway): request preprints by dated range from the newest offset", unrelated to this key; the endpoint is still present at `main` |
| Repository-wide references to the endpoint | GitHub code search: `pmc_oa` → exactly `config/external-urls.json` and `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/public_biomed_mcp.py`; `oa.fcgi` → only `config/external-urls.json`. Commit-message search for `pmc_oa` → no result, i.e. no fix commit for it |
| Observed in a real run | SD-based product run on 2026-11-09T15:49Z (see §9); reproduced against upstream sources on 2026-11-10 |

## 3. Exact source-code references

Line numbers are from `main` @ `5c765cd0`.

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| The retired endpoint, as shipped configuration | `config/external-urls.json:56` — `"pmc_oa": "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/utils/oa/oa.fcgi"` |
| The only outbound call that uses it | `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/public_biomed_mcp.py:402` — `external_url("data_sources.ncbi.pmc_oa")` inside `_pmc_pdf_candidate()` (defined at `:386`; response parsed for `.//link[@format='pdf']`, and the returned `href` must start with `data_sources.ncbi.pmc_ftp_https_prefix`, `:416`) |
| Tool entry points | `public_biomed_mcp.py:471-476` (`pubmed_prepare_paper_download`) and `:485-488` (`@SERVER.tool(name="europe-pmc_prepare_paper_download")`) |
| Transport used for the request | `public_biomed_mcp.py:97-123` `_get_text()` — `httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=TIMEOUT, follow_redirects=False)`, `accept: application/xml` |
| Endpoint status → error envelope | `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/http_errors.py:27-61` — 404 keeps `failure_scope="unknown"` (only `406` is split into `request` vs `endpoint`), then raises `RuntimeError(f"HTTP {status} {reason} from {host}" + " SOURCE_HTTP_ERROR:" + json)` |
| Envelope → model-facing code | `services/api/src/mcp/node-client.ts:238-252` (`sourceHttpFailure`), `:254-260` (`errorCodeFor`: substring `"404"` → `NOT_FOUND`), `:651-655` (`upstream`, `finalStatus`, `finalError`) |
| Why a retry never happens | `packages/data-source/src/broker.ts:700` — `retryPolicy: { ...tool.retryPolicy, maxAttempts: 1 }` ("Each governed invocation makes one attempt", `:698-699`), overriding the declared `maxAttempts: 3` in `packages/mcp-sources/src/public-biomed.ts:541-547` |
| Why the tool is reported "available" | `packages/data-source/src/catalog.ts:68-98` — `statusFor()` marks a tool available when the MCP server advertises it and the input schema is compatible; `status = missing.length ? "degraded" : "ready"`. **No provider request is made during discovery**, so a retired endpoint cannot affect readiness. |

Only two places in the repository mention this endpoint (`oa.fcgi` / `pmc_oa`): the config key and
`public_biomed_mcp.py:402`. There is no test, fixture or documentation reference to it.

## 4. Minimal reproduction

No model, no agent session and no SD deployment are required. Fetch upstream's own files verbatim
into an isolated tree and call upstream's own tool entry point.

```
# 1) take four files verbatim from main@5c765cd0 into an isolated tree and assert that each
#    recomputed git blob hash equals the blob hash the GitHub contents API reports:
#      services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/{public_biomed_mcp,external_urls,http_errors}.py
#      config/external-urls.json
#    (+ an empty src/sciencediscovery_gateway/__init__.py)
# 2) cwd = the isolated tree root, so external_urls.py resolves cwd/config/external-urls.json
#    sys.path = the isolated tree's src/
# 3) run:
```

```python
import asyncio, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "repro/src")
from sciencediscovery_gateway.public_biomed_mcp import (
    europe_pmc_prepare_paper_download, external_url)

print(external_url("data_sources.ncbi.pmc_oa"))
asyncio.run(europe_pmc_prepare_paper_download("PMC10221666"))   # isOpenAccess=Y
```

Observed (from the recorded run — request URL and status were captured by a pass-through wrapper
around `httpx.AsyncClient.send`; the wrapper only logs, it does not alter behaviour). The run also
asserts its own provenance and records it: the imported module resolved inside the isolated tree
(`under_scratch: true`), the config the loader picked was that tree's `config/external-urls.json`
(`config_is_scratch_copy: true`, chosen through the documented resolution order — env override, then
`cwd/config/…`, then module parents), and the entry point called was upstream's decorated
`europe_pmc_prepare_paper_download`, not an internal helper:

```
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/utils/oa/oa.fcgi
GET https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/utils/oa/oa.fcgi?id=PMC10221666
  -> HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found   (859 ms, server: Apache, via: 1.1 google,
                               body: "NCBI/xpmc21 - WWW Error 404 Diagnostic")
RuntimeError: HTTP 404 Not Found from www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov
  SOURCE_HTTP_ERROR:{"statusCode":404,"endpoint":"https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov","failureScope":"unknown"}
```

The same URL requested directly, without SD's code in the loop, answers the same way — we made
this request with `httpx` (GET, `accept: application/xml`, redirects not followed):

```
GET https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/utils/oa/oa.fcgi?id=PMC10221666   # 404
```

## 5. Expected behavior

For an open-access PMCID the tool returns an `artifact-plan` result with one PDF candidate
(`_pmc_pdf_candidate` builds it at `public_biomed_mcp.py:419-430`), i.e. an HTTP 2xx from the
provider locator and a `<link format="pdf">` href under the allowlisted host.

For a record that genuinely has no open-access PDF, the tool should return a *record-scoped*
outcome — the existing `ValueError("PMC OA record does not provide a PDF")` /
`"PMC OA PDF is unavailable (<code>)"` branches at `:409-417` — and the framework should present
it as "this record has no OA PDF", not as "the service is unreachable".

For an endpoint that no longer exists at the provider, the outcome should be an
**endpoint-level** failure: distinguishable from a record-level one, attributable to
`https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/utils/oa/oa.fcgi`, and surfaced to the readiness/health view.

## 6. Actual behavior

* The provider answers **HTTP 404** for both PMCID values we tried (rows A1, A2), with NCBI's own
  `xpmc21` error page.
* In the Python gateway, `http_errors.py` records a 404 with `failureScope="unknown"`: the
  `request`/`endpoint` refinement is computed only for 406 (`:44-53`). **The gateway therefore does
  not produce an endpoint-level verdict for this failure** — it emits the value that means "we did
  not classify it".
* `node-client.ts:258` then derives the model-facing code from the **message text** (`"404"`/
  `"not found"` → `NOT_FOUND`) rather than from the `failureScope` it receives and stores at `:651`
  (where, as above, the stored value is `unknown`). The result is `NOT_FOUND`, `retryable:false`,
  one attempt, and the agent sees:

```json
{"ok":false,"error":{"attempts":1,"code":"NOT_FOUND",
 "message":"HTTP 404 from https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov","retryable":false}}
```

Two things follow, and we keep them apart. **What we observed:** the identifier of an open-access
article (row A1) and that of a non-open-access one (row A2) produce the *identical* envelope above,
because the locator fails before it can say anything about the record — so the agent has no signal
with which to distinguish an outage from a gap, and behaves as if the literature were silent.
**What we are not claiming:** that SD has no record-level path; under the current code a genuinely
PDF-less record raises one of the `ValueError` branches in §5, whose text contains no `"404"` and
therefore falls through to a different code. The point is narrower, and we state it as a gap rather
than as a broken mechanism: a 404 is *not classified* in the gateway (`unknown`), and the client's
code is taken from message text instead of from that field — so neither layer currently carries an
endpoint-level verdict that the agent could act on. §10 goal 2 asks for exactly that.

## 7. Positive and negative controls

Read-only GET/HEAD. Ten recorded requests over the eight rows below, one request per distinct URL;
the failing endpoint was tried exactly twice (A1, A2) and never retried. Direct connection
(`httpx` `trust_env=True` with no `*PROXY*` variables in the environment, no mounted proxies), no
access-control workaround.

| # | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | `https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/utils/oa/oa.fcgi?id=PMC10221666` (**`isOpenAccess=Y ∧ hasPDF=Y ∧ inPMC=Y`**) | **404**, NCBI `xpmc21` error page, 859 ms |
| A2 | `https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/utils/oa/oa.fcgi?id=PMC8889753` (identifier of the real failing call, `isOpenAccess=N`) | **404**, same page, 1,312 ms |
| B | `https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10221666/` | **200**, 398,069 B — the article is live and open |
| C | `https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi?db=pmc&id=10221666&retmode=json` | **200**, 1,057 B — NCBI E-Utilities healthy |
| D | `https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?db=pmc&id=10221666&retmode=xml` | **200**, 279,585 B — NCBI serves this article's full-text XML |
| E | `https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC10221666/fullTextXML` | **200**, 286,710 B |
| F | `https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/pmc/oa_package/66/PMC10221666/` | **404**, NCBI "Object not found!" — recorded for completeness and **not** used as evidence: the `66` bucket came from a guessed directory rule that SD's code does not document, so this row says nothing about NCBI's current layout (see §11.6) |
| G | `https://pmc-oa-opendata.s3.amazonaws.com/README.txt`; `…/?prefix=PMC10221666&max-keys=40`; `HEAD …/PMC10221666.1/PMC10221666.1.pdf` | **200 / 200 / 200**, `server: AmazonS3` — NCBI's own replacement documentation (14,524 B), a bucket listing containing the key `PMC10221666.1/PMC10221666.1.pdf`, and that object at 7,690,488 B over anonymous HTTPS |

Reading of the matrix:

* **B–E are positive controls for the record and for the vendor.** The same article that 404s at
  `oa.fcgi` is served through three other routes, so neither network reachability, nor the vendor,
  nor the specific record explains the failure.
* **A2 is the negative control**, and it fails identically to A1 — which is exactly the point of
  defect 2 in §1: the current code cannot distinguish "no OA PDF for this record" from "the locator
  endpoint is gone".
* **Row G is the positive control for the *direction* of a fix**, not a prescription: a supported,
  anonymously reachable PDF object exists today for the very article `oa.fcgi` refuses (§10).
* Deliberately **not** claimed: that `efetch`/`fullTextXML` are equivalent to the OA package
  locator. They return full-text **XML**; the tool's contract is a **PDF** candidate. They are used
  here only to prove the record and the vendor are alive.

### 7.1 The seven checks this report is meant to satisfy

| Check | What it establishes | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | The retired endpoint is present in upstream's current default branch as shipped configuration | PASS | §2, §3 — `main` @ `5c765cd0`, `config/external-urls.json` blob `000f3a7721442283e45b9ae7a84a32d00451d664`, key at `:56` |
| G2 | The request that failed in a real run used that endpoint | PASS | §9 (recorded `statusCode:404`, host-level `upstream.endpoint`) + §3 (repository-wide, only two mentions of `oa.fcgi`/`pmc_oa`: the config key and `public_biomed_mcp.py:402`) |
| G3 | A positive control that is unambiguously open access fails the same way | PASS | §7/A1 — `PMC10221666`, `isOpenAccess=Y ∧ hasPDF=Y ∧ inPMC=Y` → 404 |
| G4 | Neither network conditions nor record-level absence explains the failures | PASS | §7/B–E — the same article answers 200 through three other routes |
| G5 | Upstream has not already fixed it and it still reproduces | PASS | §2 — last commit touching the file (`d79e204d4b99`, committed 2026-11-06) is unrelated to this key, and a commit-message search for `pmc_oa` returns nothing; §4 reproduced on 2026-11-10 against `5c765cd0` |
| G6 | The failure is not introduced by our fork or our environment | PASS | §8 — blob-hash comparison of eleven files across five refs, plus the override and proxy hooks checked absent |
| G7 | The remediation direction is consistent with the provider's currently documented protocol | PASS | §7/row G — NCBI's own replacement documentation and object store; §10 deliberately states goals only and leaves the implementation to the maintainers |

None of the seven is graded below PASS, and §11 lists what they do not cover.

## 8. Attribution evidence (upstream vs a downstream fork)

We run a downstream repository that vendors SD. Before reporting this we checked that the failure
is not an artifact of our fork. Eleven files on the path from configuration to model-facing error
were compared by **git blob hash** across five refs: our fork's GitHub `main`, our fork's local
`main`, our fork's release branch, a local SD snapshot (`b31f74eb`, 2026-11-06) and **upstream
`main` @ `5c765cd0` read live from GitHub**.

| Files | Result |
|---|---|
| `config/external-urls.json`, `external_urls.py`, `http_errors.py`, `node-client.ts`, `mcp-workspace-tools.ts`, `deferred-tools.ts`, `broker.ts`, `catalog.ts` | **byte-identical in all five**, including upstream's current `main` (`external-urls.json` = `000f3a7721442283e45b9ae7a84a32d00451d664`, 7,393 B) |
| `public_biomed_mcp.py`, `public-biomed.ts`, `registry.ts` | **our three refs equal upstream's current `main`**; only the local SD snapshot differs, and that snapshot is a **strict ancestor** of `main` (`compare` → `ahead_by=192, behind_by=0`), i.e. the snapshot is older, not forked |
| `git diff` of `public_biomed_mcp.py` (old snapshot → our tree) | 9 hunks, **0 of them touching** `pmc_oa`, `_pmc_pdf_candidate`, or the PDF-allowlist check |

Overrides that could have produced our own failing URL were checked and are absent:

* `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXTERNAL_URLS_PATH` (`external_urls.py:30`, the only URL-override hook) is unset
  in the process, in the Windows user and machine environments, is not in the launcher's
  `FORWARDED_RUNNER_SETTINGS`, and is never assigned by production code.
* No `*PROXY*` variable exists in the process or user/machine environment; the probes recorded
  `trust_env=True` with no mounted proxies.
* No code on our side changes `http_errors.py` or `node-client.ts`, so the flattening in §6 is
  upstream behaviour.

**Direction we do not claim**: whether those three files reached identical content by our
syncing upstream or by upstream absorbing our changes is out of scope. The point relevant to this
report is narrower: **the bytes that produced the 404 are the bytes on upstream's default branch
today**, and §4 reproduces the failure using only upstream's files.

## 9. Impact on research agents

From a recorded production run (session `93147325-9f4f-47dc-a832-532ee2b1d174`, invocation
`dd6cc808-142e-459e-a766-5c7c14a610c1`, 2026-11-09T15:49:08.582Z → 15:49:11.129Z, 1,772 ms,
`status:"semantic-error"`, `resultCount:0`):

* The agent had planned a two-step full-text route (`prepare_paper_download → paper_extract_pdf`)
  to answer a question that abstracts could not settle, called the tool correctly with
  `{"identifier":"PMC8889753"}`, and received `NOT_FOUND`.
* In the same run's retrieved set, **30 of 67 unique records** carry
  `isOpenAccess=Y ∧ hasPDF=Y ∧ inEPMC=Y ∧ inPMC=Y`, and a further 9 carry `hasPDF=Y ∧ inPMC=Y` —
  i.e. a large body of legitimately retrievable full text is unreachable through this tool today.
* The observable effect is worse than a missing download. `NOT_FOUND / retryable:false` reads as a
  **statement about the literature**, so the agent recorded "no open-access full text exists for
  this question", downgraded its own conclusions, and moved on. A maintainer reading the timeline
  sees an answered gap, not a dead endpoint.
* Because discovery readiness (`catalog.ts:68-98`) never probes the provider, the connector is
  reported `ready` while its download path is permanently broken; the readiness surface therefore
  gives no warning.
* Scope limit: this concerns the PMC OA PDF route only. Europe PMC/arXiv search and PubMed metadata
  paths in the same run worked normally, and we observed no scheduling, promotion or permission
  defect.

## 10. Suggested fix

We are not proposing an implementation — the choice is the maintainers', and we have not validated
any particular replacement API against this tool's contract. Two goals:

1. **Use a supported PMC open-access retrieval mechanism, so that a retired endpoint is not the only
   path to a PDF.** However this is done, `data_sources.ncbi.pmc_oa` should stop being a single
   point of failure for the entire download capability, and the value of that key should be
   re-checked against NCBI's current documentation rather than against the 2020-era Web Service.
   Row G of §7 is offered as evidence that *a* supported, anonymously reachable PDF object exists
   today for the article `oa.fcgi` refuses — it is not a recommended drop-in, and the caveats in
   §11.5 and §11.6 apply to it.
2. **Separate "the configured service endpoint is failing" from "this article has no open-access
   PDF",** so that neither the model nor a human reading a timeline mistakes an outage for a gap in
   the literature. SD already has the vocabulary for this distinction (`failureScope: "request" |
   "endpoint"` in `http_errors.py`), but computes it only for 406 — a 404 on this path is stored as
   `unknown`, i.e. unclassified (§6). What appears to be missing is applying that classification to
   4xx answers on a *configured API path*, and giving an endpoint-level condition somewhere the run
   can see it — `catalog.ts:68-98` never probes the provider, so readiness keeps reporting `ready`.

Both are opt-in adaptations for this one integration; neither asks SD to abandon its design choice of
keeping vendor hosts in `config/external-urls.json`, and neither is a request to restructure the
tool surface. Happy to test a candidate patch against our workload, or to share the probe harness
used in §4.

## 11. Verification limitations (what this report does not establish)

Four disclosures up front, because they bound what the evidence supports:

* **(a)** the reproduction is at function level; we did **not** complete an end-to-end run through
  SD's packaged deployment — item 1 below;
* **(b)** exactly **one** recorded real tool call stands behind §9 — item 2;
* **(c)** the full-text XML routes in §7 are **not** equivalent to the OA PDF package this tool is
  meant to locate — item 5;
* **(d)** proxy interference is excluded **only indirectly**; the state of the 2026-11-09 process was
  never recorded — item 3.

1. **Function-level, not deployment-level, reproduction.** §4 executes upstream's own gateway module
   and configuration in-process. It does not start SD's packaged stdio MCP server and Node broker.
   That transport segment is covered only by the recorded production invocation in §9.
2. **One real call.** `prepare_paper_download` was invoked exactly once in that run (and zero times
   in the sibling run). Breadth comes from the HTTP probes, not from more agent runs.
3. **The proxy state of the 2026-11-09 process is not recorded** in the invocation object, so we
   cannot assert from that record that no proxy was in play at that moment. The direct-connection
   evidence applies to the probes we ran on 2026-11-10.
4. **The response endpoint is recorded at host granularity** (`http_errors.py` deliberately reports
   `scheme://host`), so the exact failing URL is established by "single source of that URL in the
   gateway + identical envelope on reproduction", not by a full-URL field in the log.
5. **XML is not the OA package.** `efetch`/`fullTextXML` return full-text XML; the OA package
   additionally carries the licence-conditional PDF and media. The two are not interchangeable
   evidence, and §7 uses the XML routes only to show the record and the vendor are alive.
6. **`oa_package` bucket layout was not established.** Row F probes one guessed path under
   `ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov` (the host already allowlisted at `external-urls.json:57`) and it 404s;
   the guess is not evidence about NCBI's current directory scheme, and §10 deliberately does not
   rely on it.
7. **Not claimed**: that all PMC literature is undownloadable by other means; that all NCBI APIs
   fail (seven of the ten recorded requests succeeded on other routes); that the failing endpoint
   answers `404` for *every* PMCID — we tried two identifiers, one `isOpenAccess=Y` and one `=N`,
   and both returned NCBI's own 404 page; that any article *lacks* an open-access PDF on the basis
   of a 403/404 from an endpoint; or that SD has a tool-scheduling, permission or runtime defect —
   §1 and §3 cover the tool lifecycle and every stage of it worked.
8. **Provider behaviour may change again.** The NCBI notice is dated 2026-02-12 with an August 2026
   retirement; observations here are from 2026-11-09/10.

1057.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

Daily use of the desktop client (0.3.0, built from main `5c765cd0`) surfaces five places in the session UI where the interface shows something the user did not ask for, cannot act on, or cannot read. In two of them the UI *takes away* what the user is interacting with. The direction is the same in all five: keep the page terse, one short sentence where a sentence is needed, and never redraw the thing the user is clicking.

They come from four reports; the export dialog contributes two of them (list redraw and omission text).

All of them are in the desktop application (`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`); the web client carries the same research-package flows in `apps/web/src/research-package/ResearchPackageActions.tsx` and has diverged, so parity has to be checked separately. **Both locales (zh-CN and en) must change together** — each item below names the strings that exist today.

**1. Branch dialog quotes the source reply.** Opening 创建新分支聊天 shows, under the hint, a 240-character excerpt of the reply being branched from (`:326`, `…content.slice(0, 240)`). The dialog is about creating a new conversation, and the excerpt adds nothing: the hint already says what is carried over. Requested: drop the excerpt, keep the hint line.

**2. Export: selecting a workspace file empties the dialog.** In 导出会话 → 必要导出 the workspace file list lives inside `{preview ? … : null}` (`:318`), and every change to the selection resets the preview (`setPreview(undefined)` at `:220`, effect at `:217-227`) while the size is recomputed. The first checkbox click therefore unmounts the whole list — the user loses their place, cannot tick a second file until it comes back, and the dialog momentarily shows only 正在计算范围与大小… (`:317`). Computing the size is wanted; blanking the page is not.

**3. Export: 范围与省略说明 is unreadable.** The same dialog renders `preview.omissions` verbatim as a bullet list (`:319`) — internal packaging language, long, and nothing a user can act on. Requested: one or two plain sentences at most (e.g. how many versions/files are left out), or nothing.

**4. Import: the same omission list appears right after choosing a package.** `:325` renders `inspection.manifest.omissions` as a `<ul>` immediately below the file name and object count. Requested: either a single file summary line (name · objects · size) or nothing at all.

**5. After import: a second, permanent navigation entry point.** Once the research copy exists, `:301` keeps rendering `研究副本已准备好` (`t.ready`) plus an 打开会话 button (`t.open`) below the conversation. 继续聊天 already creates the copy and navigates as soon as it is ready (`:257`), so this line is a duplicate way in that never goes away. Requested: remove the ready state and its button entirely; keep only the passive 正在复制… line while the copy runs (and the failure message).

### Design Ideas

1. **Branch dialog** — render only `t.branchHint`. Delete the `<blockquote>` and the `messageId` content lookup; keep passing `messageId` for the request itself.

2. **Export file list** — keep the list mounted for the whole dialog. Split the preview into "the data the user is choosing from" (`files`, from the last successful response) and "the size being recomputed" (a pending flag). On selection change: keep `files` and the open `<details>`, mark the estimate line as recalculating, and swap in the new bytes when they arrive. Never call `setPreview(undefined)` for a selection change; a level change may still reset, since the list itself changes there.

3. **Export omissions** — replace the rendered list with a single localized summary built from counts (e.g. `{versions} 个历史版本、{files} 个未选文件未包含`), or drop the block. If a raw list is kept at all it belongs behind an explicit 详情 disclosure, not in the default view.

4. **Import inspection** — delete the omissions `<ul>`. Keep `{file.name} · {objectCount} 个内容对象` and, if useful, the payload size on the same line.

5. **Copy status** — stop rendering the `ready` branch: no 研究副本已准备好, no 打开会话. Keep `copying` (passive progress) and `failed` (error). Navigation stays exactly as it is today: 继续聊天 → the copy is created → the client jumps to it when ready, and 打开会话 as a separate affordance disappears with the line.

Copy to change in both languages: desktop `text/zh.ts` + `text/en.ts` (`ready`, `open`, `branchHint`, `omissions`, `calculating`, `files`); web `i18n/messages.ts` (`researchPackage.viewLimitations`, `researchPackage.omissions`, `researchPackage.statLimitations`, `researchPackage.previewCalculating`) for the equivalent surfaces.

### Involved Public APIs

None. All five changes are client-side rendering; the preview, inspect, import and continuation endpoints keep their current payloads. No server-side field is added or removed.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx` | Branch dialog, export dialog (file list + omissions), import inspection, copy status line |
| `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts`, `text/en.ts` | Every string above, both locales |
| `apps/desktop/src/styles/research-package.css` | Layout for the trimmed blocks |
| `apps/web/src/research-package/ResearchPackageActions.tsx` | Same flows; already refactored, verify each of the five behaviours there |
| `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` | Web strings for the same surfaces |

**Conflict to resolve before starting:** #1024 proposes *adding* per-dimension counts and an explicit "will not be restored" block to the export and import dialogs. The direction recorded here is the opposite — the user asked for fewer lines and less unexplained detail. This issue supersedes the information-density part of #1024 (its items 2, 3 and 7); #1024's export-centre and size-limit parts are unaffected. Do not implement both.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- **Component tests (desktop):** toggling a workspace file leaves the list mounted and keeps the previously known estimate visible with a pending marker; the dialog never returns to the calculating-only state on a selection change; a branch dialog renders no excerpt; an import review renders no omission list; a ready copy renders neither the ready text nor the open button.
- **E2E on the desktop build** with the real local stack, using a session that has several workspace files:
  1. 导出会话 → 必要导出 → tick file A, then tick file B without waiting: both stay ticked, the list stays open, the size settles on the value that includes both.
  2. 导出会话 → check the omissions block: at most two short lines, readable in zh-CN and en.
  3. 导入会话 → choose a package → only the summary line is shown.
  4. Import a package → 继续聊天 → land in the copy; no 研究副本已准备好 / 打开会话 line remains anywhere in the session view.
  5. Branch from an intermediate reply: the dialog shows the hint and no quoted excerpt.
- **Commands:** `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build`, `pnpm ci:l1`.
- Screenshots of all five surfaces (zh-CN and en) go in the PR body for the owner's visual approval, per the UI rule.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 创建新分支聊天 shows the hint only; no excerpt of the source reply, in both languages.
- [ ] Selecting or deselecting a workspace file never unmounts or collapses the file list, and a second file can be selected without waiting for the first recalculation.
- [ ] The size keeps recalculating in place; the dialog never replaces itself with the calculating state on a selection change.
- [ ] 范围与省略说明 is at most two plain-language lines (or removed); no internal packaging text in the default view.
- [ ] Import shows a one-line package summary (name · objects · size) and no omission list.
- [ ] After import, no 研究副本已准备好 / 打开会话 line persists; 继续聊天 navigates to the copy by itself, and failures still report.
- [ ] zh-CN and en strings both updated, no untranslated leftovers on either surface.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck|test|build` and `pnpm ci:l1` pass.
- [ ] Owner has seen the screenshots in the PR body before approval.

### Additional Information

Reported from the Windows desktop client, build `0.3.0` from main `5c765cd0` (2026-11-09T22:07Z), Simplified Chinese UI.

Related: #1024 (export UI redesign — the density items conflict, see above), #986 / PR #999 (the save flow the export dialog got in that round), #995 (import opened two sessions; item 5 here is the leftover navigation affordance from that flow), #803 (feature scope).

## Remaining heap work after #1061

#1061 fixes three whole-stream read paths in `services/api` (items 1–3 of #1011). Two things are still open: a fourth materialisation in the trajectory builder, and the measurement/budget work the original issue requires in order to show that any of this helps.

Source evidence: #1011, Nightly run [42519625781](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42519625781), shard `research-12`, main `c95f080a`. Heap died at **4126.5 MB** (the V8 default old-space limit) after **2,641,988 ms** of uptime; teardown then met `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:4410`.

### 1. `sessionTrajectory` still materialises every stream of every run

`services/api/src/trajectory.ts` (the `events: RecordedEvent[] = []` accumulator and everything it appends to, from the run loop at ~`:11` through the subagent-step loop) pushes **every event of every run, of every agent stream and every `tool-<id>` stream** into one array and returns it whole. That is the same shape of allocation #1061 removed from `listRunStreamEvents` / `exportRunStreams` / the plan panel's `state` query, one layer up: the fix in #1061 passes through this builder unchanged, because #1061 touches `plugins/control.ts`, `store.ts` and `store.test.ts` only.

Two distinct things are involved, and they are not the same work:

- **materialisation** — bound the accumulator, or stream it to the response;
- **response shape** — if the endpoint paginates or streams, the client contract changes.

### 2. The heap budget is implicit and unobservable

No launch path passes `--max-old-space-size` or `NODE_OPTIONS` (`services/api/package.json:9`, `scripts/start-stack.mjs`, `scripts/start-stack.sh`), and nothing in `services/api/src` samples `process.memoryUsage()`. The abort therefore arrives with no warning. The issue's own caution applies: raising the cap only delays the abort — what is missing is an explicit budget plus a signal before V8 kills the process.

### 3. No measurement, so no fix here is verifiable

#1011 asks for `--heapsnapshot-near-heap-limit=1`, an RSS timeline and the session's stream file sizes, "so the fix can be shown to work". Without that, #1061 reduces allocation but nobody can demonstrate that a 46-minute session no longer approaches the limit — which is why #1011 carried `need-human`.

### Why this needs a person

The cap's value and where it is set (package script vs launcher vs deployment) are operational decisions about the memory the API may use; a trajectory response-shape change is a client contract change. Both are judgement calls rather than defects with one correct answer.

### How to close this

(a) an explicit heap budget on every launch path; (b) a memory signal (log or exported timeline) so a near-limit run is visible before the process dies; (c) at least one measured long run on the new code showing the headroom; and (d) either a bounded trajectory build or a documented decision that its response is allowed to be unbounded.

Related: #1061 (stream-read fix), #1011 (original abort), #1012 (the other Nightly shard).

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** Two real-E2E evolve journeys click the send button and then wait forever for a Run that is never created. In both cases the product had already opened a **"Confirm evolution settings"** dialog, and nothing in the journey answers it.

POST /api/projects 201 Created

```

    at waitForNewRun (test/helpers/desktop-evolve.ts:377:73)
    at test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts:317:22
```

Its `stack.log` also contains no `POST /api/sessions/<id>/messages` (only `POST /api/inbox`, the workspace upload, `/api/sessions/.../runs/current/cancel` and `/cleanup/project`).

The journey reports for both shards say *"无 console 错误/警告，无失败请求"* — consistent with a dialog waiting for input rather than a failed request.

**Code.** The dialog is `apps/web/src/evolve/DirectionDialog.tsx` and, on desktop, `apps/desktop/src/views/evolve/EvolveCreateDialog.tsx`. The journeys that never answer it are `test/helpers/journeys.ts` (`sendUserMessage`), `test/helpers/desktop-evolve.ts:377` (`waitForNewRun`) and the two specs (`test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts:100`, `test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts:317`).

1. The confirmation dialog is intended product behaviour for starting an evolve search. Then both journeys are stale and must confirm the dialog (click the confirm button, then wait for the Run). Test-side fix only.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** Three real cases die within seconds to a few minutes with the same gateway message, even though the gateway had already answered `200` and was streaming:

```text
Error: Main run must complete with readable, nonempty declared final artifacts;
delivery_status=failed; run_status=failed; delivered_artifacts=0;
run_error=[181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

Shards and durations on Nightly run [42907916462](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42907916462) (sha `4bb737c2`):

| shard | case | duration |
|---|---|---|
| research-1 | DRB-58 medium-hard Swarm research integration | 51.5 s |
| research-2 | DRB-59 easy Swarm research integration | 3.9 min |
| research-5 | DRB-75 very-hard Swarm research integration | 50.8 s |

**Evidence that the stream, not the product, broke.** `stack.log` of shard `research-1` (artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-1`, id 13805059079) records that request as:

```json
[model-sse-summary] {"requestId":"model-f758639a-...","httpStatus":200,"attempts":1,"retries":0,
  "elapsedMs":29176,"sseRecords":1208,"error":{"classification":"network"}}
```

So: headers `200`, 1208 SSE records delivered over ~29 s, then the transport died; `attempts:1, retries:0` — the API never retried. The previous Nightly (`c95f080`, run 42519625781) failed the same way on `research-4` (`read ECONNRESET`) and `research-6` (`other side closed`), so this is a recurring class, not a one-off.

**Why it is scored as the product's fault.** `.ci` accounting for this run reports:

```text
Planned 21; executed 21; passed 15; provider faults 0.
```

`test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs:126-146` classifies a provider fault only when the text carries a 5xx status **or** one of `no available channel` / `model_not_found` / `new_api_error`. `APIError: read ECONNRESET` and `other side closed` carry neither, so these three failures stay plain `FAIL` and the gate treats them as regressions.

**Expected / decision needed.** Two separate questions:

1. **Retry (code):** a mid-stream transport break after `200` currently ends an 8–50 minute case. A bounded retry (one attempt, only when no tool result has been committed yet) would turn most of these into passes. This is a behaviour change and needs sign-off.
2. **Accounting (gate semantics):** should a failure whose only evidence is a broken transport, with no HTTP status, be recorded as `PROVIDER_FAULT`? Today it cannot be, and the result is a red Nightly for a provider outage.

Recommendation: land (1) as its own change and keep (2) separate, because (2) changes what "green Nightly" means.

- Same failure class on the 2026-11-08 Nightly (`c95f080`, shards `research-4`/`research-6`).

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** The mocked E2E suite is `87/88` and the one red case fails not on product behaviour but on a browser console error raised by the suite's own teardown:

```text
Error: no console/page errors expected, got:
[error] Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)
  @ http://127.0.0.1:4410/api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6/research-package/preview?sessionId=6bcfc3e0-...
```

Case: `test/agent-run-componentization.spec.ts:380` — `S2b subagent 首个受控工具的权限卡也出现在主对话最外层`. Job `Gate / L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)` (job id 130151439627) on Nightly run [42907916462](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42907916462), sha `4bb737c2`.

**Evidence.** The mocked stack's `stack.log` (in `mocked-e2e-results-standard-journeys`, artifact id 13807782121) shows the request arrives **after** the project was deleted by teardown:

```text
GET  /api/evolve/status HTTP/1.1 200 OK
DELETE /api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
POST /cleanup/project HTTP/1.1 200 OK
DELETE /api/models/4eea8f0a-... HTTP/1.1 200 OK
GET  /api/projects/3abde864-e853-4350-aa53-5ccc1a6fafa6/research-package/preview?sessionId=6bcfc3e0-...&defaults=1 HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
```

The same log carries **59** such `404` responses on `research-package/preview`, and in another case the deleted Session is still polled directly:

```text
GET /api/sessions/c6603f8c-e86e-46dd-a455-b87ff206c4fd/runs HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
GET /api/sessions/c6603f8c-e86e-46dd-a455-b87ff206c4fd/agent-activity HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
```

So the panel keeps polling a project/session that teardown has just removed. The browser logs every 404 as a console error, and the journey's "no console errors" assertion turns that into a failed case.

**Expected.** One of these, whichever the team prefers:

1. A mounted panel stops polling once its project/session is deleted (listen for the deletion the test performs, or cancel the poll on unmount).
2. The preview read treats "project gone" as a normal end of polling and does not surface it as a console error (checked request + handled 404, instead of an unhandled resource load).
3. The assertion is scoped to the case's own session being alive.

(1) is the honest fix: the product should not keep asking the API about a project it has removed.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `4bb737c2fccc8b55471dfd08f4f58754c5981cb3`.
- Mocked E2E (`profile: daily`, `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)`), 88 planned / 87 passed / 1 failed; run started 2026-11-10T21:44:15Z (2026-11-11 05:44 CST).

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Split out of #1049, which this issue does not replace: #1059 fixes the download path (the OA bucket locator and the misattributed "record not found"), and this issue is the other half of §5 — the readiness signal.

**What is still true after #1059.** `services/api/src/plugins/catalog.ts` never probes a provider. A configured integration can be completely dead — every call fails with a provider-side outage — and the readiness/health view still reports it as ready, because readiness only reads configuration, never a probe result. In that state the only way anyone learns the integration is down is an agent that actually calls the tool and reports the `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` guidance back to the user.

**Why it matters.** The issue that produced #1049 was found exactly this way: the failure was visible only in a run's tool result, not in the surface a maintainer would check first. §10 of #1049 repeats this: the product kept reporting ready while the download path was dead.

**Expected.** An endpoint-level failure that the gateway already classifies (`ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE` / `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`) should reach the readiness view, so a dead integration is visible before an agent stumbles into it. How long such a signal stays authoritative, and whether it is a probe or a last-failure timestamp, needs a decision here — the download fix in #1059 does not depend on it.

The classification this issue builds on is the one #1059 lands: `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/http_errors.py` and the broker's `upstreamError` mapping. Readiness (`catalog.ts`) is untouched by #1059 on purpose, so the two changes can be judged separately.

1084.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes the environment details and the request log needed to reproduce the failure on a real installation.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** On Windows, launching ScienceDiscovery 0.3.0 opens a maximized window with no content — a full-screen white page. Clicking the desktop icon again does not recover it: the new process exits immediately because it does not acquire the single-instance lock, and every later launch does the same. Only killing the shell process that still owns the lock lets the app start again — and it then goes white again within a few minutes once a session is open.

**What is actually failing.** The local API process (`services/api`, the Node process behind the adapter) dies of V8 heap exhaustion while research-package previews are being warmed in the background. The shell's stack supervisor (`scripts/start-stack.mjs`) sees the API child exit and tears down the adapter and the sidecars, so the UI origin on `127.0.0.1:4310` is gone while the Electron window stays alive and keeps the single-instance lock. A relaunch therefore exits as a "second instance" before any window exists, and the user has no way back into the app.

The shell log from the shipped 0.3.0 build shows this sequence twice:

```text
# crash on an already-running shell
[stack:err] FATAL ERROR: MarkCompactCollector: young object promotion failed Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
# heap at the abort: 3832.9 (3867.4) MB

# cold start, no export dialog opened by the user, crash after 284 s
[20056:00004F200011C000] 284002 ms: Scavenge 3775.5 (3806.8) -> 3730.9 (3784.6) MB ...
FATAL ERROR: MarkCompactCollector: young object promotion failed Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

After each crash, every new launch exits before creating a window:

```text
second instance: single-instance lock not acquired; exiting so the first instance stays the only one
loadUi: ui origin not answering within 30s; loading anyway (did-fail-load retry is the backstop)
```

The window state is restored as maximized, so "loading anyway" is what the user experiences as a full-screen white window.

**What produced the crash.** In the same cold-start run, the stack log shows ordinary session browsing followed by repeated full package builds. All timestamps below are from one run; IDs are redacted:

- `GET /api/sessions/<id>` for several different sessions (each of these calls `exportPreviews.watch(...)` on the server);
- **18** `POST /internal/research-package/export` calls (the memory-graph snapshot request issued once per `buildResearchPackageInput`) between 03:27:21Z and 03:30:38Z;
- `research-package/preview?level=necessary&includeFullTrajectory=0&includeFullMemoryGraph=0` at 03:30:23Z, and `level=complete&includeFullTrajectory=0&includeFullMemoryGraph=0` at 03:30:33Z;
- `FATAL ERROR ... JavaScript heap out of memory` at 03:31:35Z, 284 s after the stack started.

**Why the background warming is so heavy (confirmed in the installed build).**

1. `GET /api/sessions/:id` calls `exportPreviews.watch(projectId, sessionId)`. `watch()` calls `warm()`, and `warm()` calls `defaults()`, which computes **five** preview profiles per session: `necessary`; `complete`; `complete + full trajectory`; `complete + full memory graph`; `complete + both`. A plain session read is therefore enough to start five full export builds.
2. Every profile runs `buildResearchPackageInput` from scratch. For every session in the dependency closure it materialises all messages, all runs, **every event of every run stream**, workspace files and provenance, all artifact versions, reviews and audit tasks, export history, claims and evidence, plus a memory-graph snapshot. The `necessary` filter is applied **after** this load, so the "small" profile pays the full materialisation cost.
3. `sessionTrajectory` reads the same run streams a second time to build the trajectory index. `complete + full trajectory` then hydrates every trajectory detail into a single array.
4. The preview path only avoids reading CAS payload bytes. Every metadata object above is still resident at the same time.
5. Builds are serialised on one queue, so the five profiles run back to back and the previous build's garbage has not been collected when the next one starts. `tick()` repeats the warm for watched sessions every 3 s.
6. No launch path sets `--max-old-space-size` or `NODE_OPTIONS`, so the process aborts at the Node default old-space limit (about 4 GB).

On this installation (about 2.7 GB of project data and 3 GB of versioning/CAS data), two preview profiles raised the API process from about 164 MB to about 949 MB of private bytes, and a third request for `complete + includeFullTrajectory=1` killed it. That is consistent with the 4–5 minute crash above.

**What I expected.** Opening the app and browsing sessions should not start a full export build. Preview work should be bounded, should run when the user opens the export dialog, and a dead API should not leave the desktop shell stuck on a white window that cannot be relaunched.

**Suggested direction.**

- Do not warm previews from `GET /api/sessions/:id`; warm on export-dialog open only, and at most one profile at a time.
- Apply the `necessary` filter while streaming, or before loading run streams, and make run-stream reads cursor-based (the same direction as #1011).
- Skip the warm when the revision is unchanged (the cache key exists, but the first warm of each revision still runs five builds).
- Give the shell a failure path: if the stack dies while the window is open, surface an actionable error and allow a restart instead of holding the single-instance lock over a dead origin.
- Make the heap budget explicit and observable on every launch path.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- OS: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045, x64.
- ScienceDiscovery desktop 0.3.0 (win-x64 installer), local mode via `start-stack.mjs --mode local --no-node-build`. No `NODE_OPTIONS` or `--max-old-space-size` in the environment or in the launch scripts.
- Data directory: about 2.7 GB of projects, 3 GB of versioning/CAS, 38 MB of run-event streams. The project involved contains several sessions, including a long-running session with tool and subagent streams.
- The failure was reproduced twice: once on a shell that had already been running, and once from a cold start, without opening the export dialog in either case.

### Additional Information

- Related but not duplicates: #1011 reports the same class of heap growth in a long real session, but its user-visible symptom is teardown `ECONNREFUSED`; the trigger reported here is preview warming on a plain session read, and the symptom is a white window that cannot be relaunched. #1079 / #1083 report a failed preview for `complete + includeFullTrajectory`; on this installation that exact request kills the API instead of returning 404. #1024 covers the export dialog redesign; this issue is about the runtime cost behind the preview.
- The analysis was done against the shipped 0.3.0 build, so file/line locations should be confirmed against `main`.
- Session and project identifiers and local paths are redacted on purpose.

### Version Information

- ScienceDiscovery 0.3.0.0 (win-x64), build dated 2026-11-10.
- Electron/Node as shipped with that installer; the aborts occurred at 3.8–4.1 GB of V8 heap, the default old-space limit.
